title: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis treatment
bottleneck: Drug-resistant TB requires 6 to 20 months of treatment with toxic, expensive regimens, and rifampicin-resistant TB is a WHO critical priority. Treatment success for multidrug-resistant TB remains far below that of drug-susceptible disease, while 40% of pipeline antibiotics target TB and other critical pathogens are neglected.
why_it_blocks: TB kills over a million people yearly; drug resistance threatens to return treatment to the pre-antibiotic era for the world's deadliest bacterial infection.
current_state: Shorter all-oral bedaquiline-based regimens have improved outcomes, but access gaps, diagnostic delays, and emerging resistance to the new drugs themselves keep multidrug-resistant TB a crisis. Shorter regimens have improved completion rates, but drug-resistant TB still demands months of toxic therapy that many health systems struggle to deliver. Preventing resistance through better first-line treatment completion is as important as developing new drugs.
